public_rationale: The claim is a hedged generalisation. 'Pretty hard' has no threshold, and 'stands out' has no measure. It sets aside fine-tuning, which is the main known way to steer a model, and says that fine-tuning only 'likely' costs accuracy. Rozado's study shows that models cluster left of center and that modest fine-tuning can move them. That fits the claim's framing, but it cannot confirm or refute 'pretty hard', and it gives no accuracy data. No reading an informed reader would share turns this into a testable claim.
limitations: Only one main study reviewed in depth.
Prompt-based steering (system prompts) was not assessed as a possible counterexample.

conditions: if you use the same data as everyone else

statement.excerpt: Short of using some fine-tuning tricks that likely reduce accuracy, it’s actually pretty hard to make an LLM that stands out from the pack – if you use the same data as everyone else.

from_speaker: pretty hard to make an LLM that stands out from the pack
if you use the same data as everyone else
short of using some fine-tuning tricks
our_interpretation: This is a general claim about how hard something is. It has two built-in hedges: 'pretty hard' and fine-tuning that 'likely' reduces accuracy.
It sets aside fine-tuning, which is the main known way to shift a model's views. It names no measure of 'standing out' and no amount of accuracy lost. So no study result could clearly show it false.
criteria.support_condition: Would need evidence that models trained on shared web data cannot be made to differ much (for example in political lean) except through fine-tuning, and that such fine-tuning measurably lowers accuracy.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Would need evidence that models trained on the same data are routinely and easily made to differ sharply, by means other than fine-tuning or by fine-tuning that costs no accuracy.

evidence.excerpt: LLMs can be steered towards specific locations in the political spectrum through Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) with only modest amounts of politically aligned data
evidence.explanation: Shows that fine-tuning can cheaply make a model stand out politically. The claim already exempts fine-tuning, and this study gives no accuracy-cost result. So it gives context, not a verdict.
